root_cause.text: The `usb_anchor` structure was allocated using device-managed memory bound to the parent USB device instead of the USB interface, preventing automatic cleanup when the driver is unbound.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies `rt2x00usb_probe` to change `devm_kmalloc(&usb_dev->dev, ...)` to `devm_kmalloc(&usb_intf->dev, ...)`, ensuring the resource lifetime is tied to the USB interface which the driver binds to, as described in the commit message.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by modifying the device pointer in devm_kmalloc from the parent device to the USB interface, ensuring proper resource cleanup aligned with the interface lifecycle.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement assigns the USB interface device to rt2x00dev->dev. According to the vulnerability root cause, the usb_anchor structure was allocated using device-managed memory bound to the parent USB device instead of the USB interface. When the driver is unbound, the device-managed cleanup mechanism relies on this device pointer. If the usb_anchor initialization used this incorrectly bound device reference (pointing to parent rather than interface), the anchor would not be properly cleaned up during driver unbind, leading to resource leaks and potential use-after-free vulnerabilities.
